key_insight: TurboVLA replaces the standard vision-to-language-to-action pipeline with a more direct vision-plus-language-to-action mapping, cutting latency and memory use dramatically. The result is a real-time VLA system that runs at 32 Hz on an RTX 4090 while using less than 1 GB of VRAM.
problem_solved: Traditional VLA models are too slow and memory-intensive for real-time robot control because they route visual inputs through a large language model at every step. This creates high compute overhead and limits deployment on practical hardware.
method: Reformulates the classic V -> L -> A pipeline into a direct V + L -> A mapping to reduce intermediate computation.
Reduces reliance on heavy LLM-centric processing during each policy invocation, lowering both latency and VRAM usage.
Targets efficient inference for robot action prediction on consumer-grade GPU hardware.
impact: This work makes real-time robot policy execution more practical by showing that high-frequency VLA inference can run on a single RTX 4090 with minimal memory. For practitioners, it points toward deployable embodied AI systems that are faster, cheaper, and easier to scale.

paper_title: TurboVLA: Real-Time Vision-Language-Action Model at 32 Hz on an RTX 4090 with <1 GB VRAM
paper_authors: Hengyi Xie, Chenfei Yao, Xianjin Wu, Xuanyang Xi, Yiping Tang
